summary: Computers store data as bits, so we use base 2 (binary) and base 16 (hexadecimal) to represent numbers.
Binary places correspond to powers of 2, while hexadecimal digits represent exactly 4 bits.
Converting between bases involves grouping binary digits or using arithmetic for decimal conversions.

points.text: Computers store bits, so we use base 2 or base 16 to see what is in memory.
Each binary place represents a power of 2, increasing from right to left as 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
The binary number 1101 equals 11 in decimal.
Hexadecimal uses digits 0-9 and A-F, meaning one hex digit is exactly 4 bits.
The hexadecimal number 0x2F equals 46 in decimal.
To convert binary to hex, split the bits into groups of four from the right and swap each group for a hex digit.
0xFF is 255 in decimal, which is the largest number one byte can hold.

concepts.name: Binary
concepts.definition: A number system with base 2, using only digits 0 and 1. Each position represents a power of 2.
points: Each binary place is a power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 going right to left.
gotchas: People often wonder why we bother with hex instead of just reading binary directly.

concepts.name: Hexadecimal
concepts.definition: A number system with base 16, using digits 0-9 and letters A-F. One hex digit represents exactly 4 bits.
points: Hex uses 0-9 then A-F, so one hex digit is exactly 4 bits.

concepts.name: Decimal
concepts.definition: The standard number system humans use, with base 10. It is the target for most conversions.

concepts.name: Byte
concepts.definition: A unit of digital information consisting of 8 bits. The maximum value it can hold is 255 (0xFF).

claims.claim: Computers only store bits, so we write numbers in base 2 or base 16 to see what's actually in memory.
Each binary place is a power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 going right to left.
Hex uses 0-9 then A-F, so one hex digit is exactly 4 bits.
Binary to hex: split the bits into groups of 4 from the right and swap each group for one hex digit.
0xFF is 255, the biggest number one byte can hold.

answers.answer: Yes. You can convert decimal to hex in your head by repeatedly dividing the number by 16 and noting the remainders. For example, 46 divided by 16 is 2 with a remainder of 14 (E), so 46 becomes 2E.

explanations.explanation: We use hexadecimal because it is a compact way to represent binary data. Since one hex digit equals four bits, a single byte (8 bits) can be written as just two hex characters. This makes reading and writing memory addresses much easier than using long strings of 0s and 1s.

processes.title: Converting Binary to Hexadecimal
steps: Split the bits into groups of four starting from the right.
Convert each group of four bits to its corresponding hex digit.
Combine the hex digits to form the final result.
